# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis
**Evidence file:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, 1962.2s / ~32.7 min capture, LAN `10.8.15.0/24`)
**No other artifacts (IDS/Suricata alerts) were present in the evidence directory — this analysis is derived entirely from the packet capture.**

## 1. Infected Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** | DHCP lease, all subsequent traffic |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (Intel NIC) | DHCP Discover/Request frames, ARP |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** | DHCP option 12, NBNS name registration, mDNS query, LLMNR query |
| AD domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU / `lafontainebleu.org` | NBNS, DNS SRV lookups (`_ldap._tcp...lafontainebleu.org`) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **plucero** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString from 10.8.15.133 to the domain controller (alongside the machine account `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$`) |

## 2. Malware Family and Attribution

**Attribution basis: behavioral/TTP, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/IDS/YARA alert exists in the provided evidence (only the raw pcap was supplied), so no formal signature match can be claimed. The chain below is reconstructed purely from packet-level observation.

**Infection chain observed:**

1. **t≈74.7s** — HTTP GET to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70) returns a 2.77 MB ZIP archive (`sha256: 798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5`) containing a single file, **`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`** (6,990,020 bytes, `sha256: dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c`). The JS is padded with megabytes of unrelated benign filler text (scraped-looking report/document content) to inflate its size — a well-known evasion technique used by fake-invoice JS downloaders of the **GootLoader** class. This is the strongest behavioral signal for family classification, but it is inferential, not a hash/signature hit against a known-bad database.
2. **t≈135.9s** — Windows BITS (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`) fetches `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — a 159,232-byte PE32+ DLL (`sha256: b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`). This binary self-identifies via its embedded debug path: `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb` (internal module name `release.dll`), and exports `DllRegisterServer`, `DllRegisterServerEx`, `DllGetClassObject`, `DllUnregisterServer` — i.e., it is built to be invoked via `regsvr32.exe`/COM registration (a documented defense-evasion LOLBin technique, MITRE T1218.010). I'm labeling this component **"Knock" loader/backdoor** based on its own self-identifying build string; I have no independent signature database to confirm this matches a named, tracked malware family, so treat the name as descriptive rather than confirmed attribution.
3. **t≈196s → 1962s (end of capture)** — Sustained C2 beaconing: **303** HTTP `GET /` requests from 10.8.15.133 to 72.5.43.29:80, at roughly 5–7 second intervals, using a distinctive non-browser User-Agent string `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the malformed spacing "Mozilla / 5.0", inconsistent with any real browser). Most responses are small (94–124 byte) `400 Bad Request` bodies, consistent with idle/no-tasking beacon check-ins.

**Note on a discarded lead:** intermediate BITS transfers from the legitimate Microsoft Delivery Optimization CDN (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, 199.232.210.172) were also observed around t≈102–127s, content-typed `application/x-chrome-extension`, 15KB and 171KB respectively. These are Microsoft-hosted, small, and do not correlate with any malicious string/hash in this capture — I could not confirm they are part of the attack chain and am not including them as IOCs.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (grounded in this capture only)

**C2 endpoint:**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — hardcoded IP, no DNS lookup performed (confirms it is not resolved via a domain), used both to serve the loader DLL and for ongoing beacon traffic.

**Malicious domains:**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved to 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 — Cloudflare-fronted) — hosted the invoice ZIP/JS downloader.
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (same resolved IPs) — queried via DNS and contacted over TLS (present in TLS SNI); no plaintext HTTP request body was captured for this host.

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215`
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`

**Transferred files / hashes:**

| File | Size | SHA256 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZIP delivered from FedEx-lure domain (unnamed by the site; underlying filename below) | 2,767,804 B | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | quote.checkfedexexp.com |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (contents of above ZIP) | 6,990,020 B | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | inside ZIP |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ DLL, internal name `release.dll` / `knock.pdb`) | 159,232 B | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | 72.5.43.29 |

## Summary

Host **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as domain user **plucero** on the LAFONTAINEBLEU AD domain, retrieved a fake-invoice ZIP/JS downloader from `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, which subsequently triggered a BITS-driven download of a COM-registrable loader DLL ("Knock", per its own PDB path) from a hardcoded C2 IP (72.5.43.29:80). The host then beaconed to that C2 IP roughly every 5–7 seconds for the remainder of the 32-minute capture (303 check-ins). Family attribution to GootLoader/associated loader tooling is behavioral (delivery TTP and build-string match) rather than signature-confirmed, since no IDS/AV artifacts accompanied this pcap.
